page: Amazon Web Services m3.medium is a general-purpose, previous-generation instance hosted on the Xen hypervisor. It is configured with a single dedicated vCPU mapped to 1 physical core running at a nominal base frequency of 2.5 GHz on an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor (Ivy Bridge architecture). The instance is allocated 4.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio common in general-purpose virtual machines. It also bundles 4 GB of local SSD instance storage, while lacking discrete GPU acceleration and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements place the computing and memory capabilities in the lower performance tiers when evaluated against modern cloud platforms. The single-threaded and multi-threaded stress-ng scores both plateau at 1259.98, reflecting the strict single-core footprint. Geekbench scores sit at 668.0 for single-core and 669.0 for multi-core, with PassMark reporting a CPU score of 1448.04 and a memory score of 837.38. Instruction set support includes baseline AVX and AES extensions, but lacks modern AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions, resulting in constrained performance during cryptographic operations (PassMark encryption of 484.21) and software builds (Geekbench clang score of 1260.0).

Throughput tests indicate modest capabilities across I/O and operational workloads. Memory bandwidth sustains 11.78 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 10.36 GB/sec for writes. Application tests record Redis SET performance at 0.61 million operations per second, with static web serving yielding 1.47 GB/sec throughput. Lightweight inference utilizing a small 135M model processes prompts at 47.93 tokens per second and generates text at 28.2 tokens per second.

From an operational tradeoff perspective, the m3.medium hardware profile reflects older enterprise equipment. The presence of bundled local SSD storage allows basic ephemeral caching without remote block storage overhead. Given the limited single-core throughput and legacy architecture, m3.medium fits non-critical services, legacy workload maintenance, light staging environments, and basic background tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m3.medium is a legacy general-purpose instance featuring 1 dedicated vCPU on an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM. Running on the Xen hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, it incorporates 4 GB of local SSD ephemeral storage, no GPU hardware, and a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks reflect its legacy hardware generation, achieving a Geekbench score of 668.0, a PassMark CPU score of 1448.04, and uncached large-block read memory bandwidth of 11.78 GB/sec. Application testing shows 0.61 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.47 GB/sec in static web serving. While offering dedicated core execution without burstable throttling, its generational profile makes it suited primarily for legacy maintenance, basic dev/test environments, and low-traffic internal utilities.
